# ScheduleGenerator documentation

## What this system is

The system document has not been written yet, so there is no architectural overview to

## Components

| Component | Owns | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [About](../frontend/src/app/about/DOCS/About.md) | `frontend/src/app/about` | The about unit owns the About page for the Tuks Schedule Generator service. It introduces the developer behind the tool, states the zero-data-policy, and links to the project's open-source repository and a contact email. The page is static and presentational, rendering fixed content with no data fetching (inference: the unit holds a single presentational component). <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/about/DOCS/About.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-about.0ed6fab4)</sup> |
| [App](../frontend/src/app/DOCS/App.md) | `frontend/src/app` | The app root unit owns the frontend entry point of the Tuks Schedule Generator: the root layout that wraps every page, the landing page that introduces the service, and the global stylesheet that defines the visual theme. A dependant can rely on a consistent page shell, document metadata, and light and dark theming across the application. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/DOCS/App.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app.415ff023)</sup> |
| [Auth](../frontend/src/components/auth/DOCS/Auth.md) | `frontend/src/components/auth` | The auth components unit owns the sign-in and account UI of the Tuks Schedule Generator frontend: GoogleLoginButton, a Google OAuth sign-in button that delegates the login action and loading state to the useAuth hook, and UserAvatar, a user avatar with a logout dropdown, re-exported with their prop types from a single barrel module. A dependant can rely on a branded Google sign-in entry point and a user menu for signing out. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/components/auth/DOCS/Auth.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-auth.303282e0)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/components/auth/DOCS/Auth.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-auth.bb264047)</sup> <sup>[3](../frontend/src/components/auth/DOCS/Auth.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-auth.3458c6e3)</sup> |
| [Auth dto](../backend/src/auth/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/auth/dto` | The dto unit owns the request and response shapes the auth module exchanges with its callers. It defines eight exported DTO classes across two files: the user, authentication status, and response shapes of the auth flow, and the request and response shapes of the IP-blocking flow. <sup>[1](../backend/src/auth/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-dto.06c54672)</sup> Dependants can rely on these classes to carry Swagger-documented payloads between the auth controller and its clients. <sup>[2](../backend/src/auth/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-dto.72901a78)</sup> |
| [Auth guards](../backend/src/auth/guards/DOCS/Guards.md) | `backend/src/auth/guards` | The guards unit owns the two route guards of the auth module: GoogleAuthGuard, which runs the Google OAuth flow and records failed attempts, and IpBlockingGuard, which rejects requests from blocked IPs. Both depend on IpBlockingService. Dependants can rely on these guards to protect auth routes from unauthenticated and blocked-IP access. <sup>[1](../backend/src/auth/guards/DOCS/Guards.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-guards.4eafa1c9)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/auth/guards/DOCS/Guards.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-guards.0a33100e)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/auth/guards/DOCS/Guards.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-guards.5f7d220b)</sup> |
| [Backend](../backend/DOCS/Backend.md) | `backend` | The backend unit is the ScheduleGenerator's server application: a private NestJS application named 'backend' that compiles strict TypeScript to ./dist and ships as a containerized service on port 3001. <sup>[1](../backend/DOCS/Backend.evidence.md#research.backend.e5c8e0f5)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/DOCS/Backend.evidence.md#research.backend.a9b5c807)</sup> A dependant can rely on the standard npm lifecycle — build, start, lint, test — and on a Fly.io deployment that serves the API over HTTPS. <sup>[3](../backend/DOCS/Backend.evidence.md#research.backend.150705f1)</sup> <sup>[4](../backend/DOCS/Backend.evidence.md#research.backend.ac621e01)</sup> |
| [Cache](../backend/src/cache/DOCS/Cache.md) | `backend/src/cache` | The cache unit owns the application's shared cache. It exposes a single NestJS module, CacheModule, that registers a global cache with a five-minute default TTL and a one-thousand-item limit. <sup>[1](../backend/src/cache/DOCS/Cache.evidence.md#research.backend-src-cache.7f2e5345)</sup> Any module that imports CacheModule can use the cache, and the root AppModule already does, making the cache available across the application. <sup>[2](../backend/src/cache/DOCS/Cache.evidence.md#research.backend-src-cache.3854dd3f)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/cache/DOCS/Cache.evidence.md#research.backend-src-cache.c6629710)</sup> |
| [Calendar dto](../backend/src/calendar/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/calendar/dto` | The dto unit owns the request and response shapes the calendar module exchanges with its callers. It defines the calendar module's data-transfer objects across four files: the event configuration, add-events, calendar-list, and ICS-generation shapes of the calendar flow. <sup>[1](../backend/src/calendar/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-calendar-dto.acc9046f)</sup> Dependants can rely on these classes to carry Swagger-documented, validated payloads between the calendar controller and its clients. <sup>[2](../backend/src/calendar/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-calendar-dto.d65e12ed)</sup> |
| [Common](../frontend/src/components/common/DOCS/Common.md) | `frontend/src/components/common` | The common components unit owns the shared UI primitives of the Tuks Schedule Generator frontend: Alert, Button, Card, Loading, and Modal, re-exported with their prop types from a single barrel module. A dependant can rely on a consistent set of DaisyUI-styled building blocks for status messages, actions, content containers, loading states, and dialogs across the application. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/components/common/DOCS/Common.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-common.4c93d27b)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/components/common/DOCS/Common.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-common.71789013)</sup> |
| [Common dto](../backend/src/common/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/common/dto` | The dto unit owns the application's shared error-response shape. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-dto.d70f62b4)</sup> It defines a single class, ErrorResponseDto, that describes the JSON body of an HTTP error response with three required fields — statusCode, message, and timestamp — and two optional fields — path and details. <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-dto.3dc17d40)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/common/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-dto.de431570)</sup> The jobs and upload controllers use ErrorResponseDto as the type of their @ApiResponse error responses, so API documentation and clients see one consistent error shape. <sup>[4](../backend/src/common/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-dto.8be4350b)</sup> |
| [Common guards](../backend/src/common/guards/DOCS/Guards.md) | `backend/src/common/guards` | The guards unit owns the application's HTTP rate limiting. It exports CustomThrottlerGuard, an @Injectable() guard that extends ThrottlerGuard from @nestjs/throttler and attaches rate limit information to every response so the RateLimitHeadersInterceptor can add the appropriate headers. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/guards/DOCS/Guards.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-guards.331a91ed)</sup> AppModule registers it as a global guard, so every request in the application is throttled. <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/guards/DOCS/Guards.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-guards.03354d0c)</sup> |
| [Config](../backend/src/config/DOCS/Config.md) | `backend/src/config` | The config unit owns the application's configuration. It exposes a single NestJS module, AppConfigModule, that registers the @nestjs/config ConfigModule as a global module, loading a configuration factory that reads environment variables with fallback defaults and exporting ConfigModule for any importing module. <sup>[1](../backend/src/config/DOCS/Config.evidence.md#research.backend-src-config.f3479eba)</sup> The root AppModule imports AppConfigModule, making the configuration available across the application. <sup>[2](../backend/src/config/DOCS/Config.evidence.md#research.backend-src-config.0b0b5327)</sup> |
| [Exceptions](../backend/src/upload/exceptions/DOCS/Exceptions.md) | `backend/src/upload/exceptions` | The exceptions unit owns the upload module's storage-quota error type. It defines a single exception, StorageQuotaExceededException, that upload code throws when a file exceeds the per-file size limit, and that surfaces to callers as an HTTP 413 Payload Too Large response carrying the usage, quota, and file size that caused the rejection. <sup>[1](../backend/src/upload/exceptions/DOCS/Exceptions.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-exceptions.4ca6495a)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/upload/exceptions/DOCS/Exceptions.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-exceptions.eacb61cc)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/upload/exceptions/DOCS/Exceptions.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-exceptions.6e62d2af)</sup> |
| [Filters](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.md) | `backend/src/common/filters` | The filters unit owns the application's global exception handling. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-filters.1f111551)</sup> It provides a single class, HttpExceptionFilter, that catches every exception raised in the application, turns it into a consistent HTTP error response, and logs it with request context. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-filters.1f111551)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-filters.4bfeab06)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-filters.bda5b518)</sup> Registered as a global filter, it applies to every request in the application. <sup>[4](../backend/src/common/filters/DOCS/Filters.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-filters.2b8aaaa3)</sup> |
| [Frontend](../frontend/DOCS/Frontend.md) | `frontend` | The frontend unit is the application shell of the Schedule Generator web app: a private Next.js application named 'frontend' (version 0.1.0) that owns the build, test, lint, container, and deployment configuration for the user interface. It declares the React runtime, Tailwind CSS tooling, and Vitest test setup that the application's pages and components are built, tested, and shipped with. <sup>[1](../frontend/DOCS/Frontend.evidence.md#research.frontend.203241bb)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/DOCS/Frontend.evidence.md#research.frontend.4a63769d)</sup> <sup>[3](../frontend/DOCS/Frontend.evidence.md#research.frontend.7363fcd8)</sup> |
| [Hooks](../frontend/src/hooks/DOCS/Hooks.md) | `frontend/src/hooks` | The frontend/src/hooks unit owns the React hooks that connect the Tuks Schedule Generator's pages to its state stores and services: authentication, PDF upload, job status, Google Calendar management, and workflow guarding. A dependant can rely on a consistent, store-backed interface for these concerns without reaching into the stores or services directly. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/hooks/DOCS/Hooks.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-hooks.4201f24c)</sup> |
| [Interceptors](../backend/src/common/interceptors/DOCS/Interceptors.md) | `backend/src/common/interceptors` | The interceptors unit owns the backend's cross-cutting HTTP request handling: three NestJS interceptors that log every request with timing, bound request duration with a configurable timeout, and attach rate-limit headers to responses. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/interceptors/DOCS/Interceptors.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-interceptors.a9c23c83)</sup> Dependants can rely on consistent request logging, a bounded request duration, and rate-limit information on responses without per-controller wiring. <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/interceptors/DOCS/Interceptors.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-interceptors.30699c65)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/common/interceptors/DOCS/Interceptors.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-interceptors.18251310)</sup> <sup>[4](../backend/src/common/interceptors/DOCS/Interceptors.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-interceptors.61a7a445)</sup> |
| [Jobs](../backend/src/jobs/DOCS/Jobs.md) | `backend/src/jobs` | The jobs unit owns the HTTP surface for PDF-processing jobs: the controller that serves job status and parsed-event results, the service behind it, and the module wiring that registers both. <sup>[1](../backend/src/jobs/DOCS/Jobs.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs.15c336b3)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/jobs/DOCS/Jobs.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs.bffe2d79)</sup> Dependants can rely on the two api/jobs endpoints, the JobsService provider, and the barrel re-exports that expose the feature to the application root. <sup>[3](../backend/src/jobs/DOCS/Jobs.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs.8217c5a9)</sup> <sup>[4](../backend/src/jobs/DOCS/Jobs.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs.e390b3e8)</sup> |
| [Jobs dto](../backend/src/jobs/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/jobs/dto` | The dto unit owns the request and response shapes the jobs module exchanges with its callers. It defines three exported DTO classes across two files: the parsed-event and job-result shapes of the PDF-parsing flow, and the job-status shape of the job lifecycle. <sup>[1](../backend/src/jobs/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs-dto.3ca8491a)</sup> Dependants can rely on these classes to carry Swagger-documented payloads between the jobs controller and its clients. <sup>[2](../backend/src/jobs/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-jobs-dto.f0a084ca)</sup> |
| [Parser](../backend/src/parser/DOCS/Parser.md) | `backend/src/parser` | The parser unit owns ParserModule and ParserService, the NestJS module and service that send PDF schedule files to the Python parser worker and translate the worker's response into the backend's ParsedEvent shape. <sup>[1](../backend/src/parser/DOCS/Parser.evidence.md#research.backend-src-parser.e56b44bf)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/parser/DOCS/Parser.evidence.md#research.backend-src-parser.87f7fa81)</sup> A dependant can rely on ParserService.parsePdf accepting a PDF buffer and a PdfType and returning a normalized array of parsed events. <sup>[3](../backend/src/parser/DOCS/Parser.evidence.md#research.backend-src-parser.1512ef80)</sup> |
| [Parser dto](../backend/src/parser/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/parser/dto` | The parser DTO unit owns ParsedEventDto, the data transfer object that represents a parsed event. <sup>[1](../backend/src/parser/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-parser-dto.acf782fb)</sup> It defines the event's shape — a unique identifier, module code, activity type, optional group, day and date, start and end times, venue, and a recurring flag — and validates each field with class-validator rules. <sup>[2](../backend/src/parser/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-parser-dto.e0cd8a63)</sup> |
| [Pipes](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.md) | `backend/src/common/pipes` | The pipes unit owns the shared file-validation pipe for uploads. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-pipes.583c665f)</sup> It defines FileValidationPipe, a NestJS pipe that rejects missing files, non-PDF files, and files over 10MB before they reach the upload handler, and returns valid files unchanged. <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-pipes.1da762c0)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-pipes.b3934f5d)</sup> <sup>[4](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-pipes.5d2f6012)</sup> <sup>[5](../backend/src/common/pipes/DOCS/Pipes.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-pipes.43edab1e)</sup> Upload dependants can rely on one consistent validation gate for PDF uploads. |
| [Preview](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.md) | `frontend/src/components/preview` | The preview components unit owns the schedule preview UI of the Tuks Schedule Generator frontend: EventList, a day-grouped, filterable list of selectable event cards, EventFilter, a module filter dropdown, and BulkActions, a Select All / Deselect All control with a selection count, re-exported with their prop types from a single barrel module. A dependant can rely on a filterable, selectable schedule preview with bulk selection and unfinalised-exam warnings. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-preview.28920490)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-preview.97fd0b5a)</sup> <sup>[3](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-preview.67168661)</sup> <sup>[4](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-preview.7c45d4cc)</sup> <sup>[5](../frontend/src/components/preview/DOCS/Preview.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-components-preview.8d2e31a0)</sup> |
| [Privacy](../frontend/src/app/privacy/DOCS/Privacy.md) | `frontend/src/app/privacy` | The privacy unit owns the Privacy Policy page of the Tuks Schedule Generator: a static, presentational page that explains how the service collects, uses, stores, and protects personal data. A dependant can rely on a complete, self-contained policy document covering data collection, retention, security, third-party services, user rights, and contact details, with no runtime behaviour of its own. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/privacy/DOCS/Privacy.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-privacy.06d54963)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/app/privacy/DOCS/Privacy.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-privacy.a786a279)</sup> |
| [Storage Test](../frontend/src/app/demo/storage-test/DOCS/Storage_Test.md) | `frontend/src/app/demo/storage-test` | The storage-test unit owns a single demo page that exercises the session-state-persistence feature: it triggers toast notifications, writes to the event and config stores, clears workflow and all state, and probes sessionStorage quota and disabled-storage behaviour, recording each outcome in an on-page result log. A maintainer can rely on it as a manual harness for storage error handling. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/demo/storage-test/DOCS/Storage_Test.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-demo-storage-test.97daf1d3)</sup> |
| [Strategies](../backend/src/auth/strategies/DOCS/Strategies.md) | `backend/src/auth/strategies` | The strategies unit owns the backend's Google OAuth authentication strategy. It defines GoogleStrategy, the Passport strategy named 'google', which verifies Google profiles and produces a session user through the auth service. <sup>[1](../backend/src/auth/strategies/DOCS/Strategies.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-strategies.e20cc20a)</sup> Dependants can rely on it to turn a verified Google login into a session user with calendar access. <sup>[2](../backend/src/auth/strategies/DOCS/Strategies.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-strategies.c71fd0cb)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/auth/strategies/DOCS/Strategies.evidence.md#research.backend-src-auth-strategies.74adf96b)</sup> |
| [Terms](../frontend/src/app/terms/DOCS/Terms.md) | `frontend/src/app/terms` | The terms unit owns the Terms of Service page for the Tuks Schedule Generator service. It renders a static, presentational page that states the service's terms: what the tool does, user responsibilities, Google Calendar access, data processing and privacy, accuracy and verification, liability limits, and the remaining legal provisions. The page takes no props, holds no state, and performs no data fetching. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/terms/DOCS/Terms.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-terms.118f95e7)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/app/terms/DOCS/Terms.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-terms.709797fa)</sup> |
| [Upload](../frontend/src/app/upload/DOCS/Upload.md) | `frontend/src/app/upload` | The upload unit owns the page where a user submits a UP PDF schedule: it collects the file, uploads it through the API, shows progress, and hands the parsed events to the preview step. A dependant can rely on a single page that drives the upload lifecycle from file selection through completion and redirects to /preview after a successful upload. <sup>[1](../frontend/src/app/upload/DOCS/Upload.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-upload.1dfb9cdd)</sup> <sup>[2](../frontend/src/app/upload/DOCS/Upload.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-upload.ec70049a)</sup> <sup>[3](../frontend/src/app/upload/DOCS/Upload.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-upload.e1e0b822)</sup> <sup>[4](../frontend/src/app/upload/DOCS/Upload.evidence.md#research.frontend-src-app-upload.4b13b959)</sup> |
| [Upload dto](../backend/src/upload/dto/DOCS/Dto.md) | `backend/src/upload/dto` | The dto unit owns the upload module's data-transfer types: the response shape for the upload endpoint, the storage-usage report, and the storage-quota error body. Dependants can rely on these classes to carry the upload result, usage figures, and quota-exceeded details consistently across the controller, service, and exception layers. <sup>[1](../backend/src/upload/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-dto.af8a9e0e)</sup> <sup>[2](../backend/src/upload/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-dto.0f841c82)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/upload/dto/DOCS/Dto.evidence.md#research.backend-src-upload-dto.7ff4b838)</sup> |
| [Validators](../backend/src/common/validators/DOCS/Validators.md) | `backend/src/common/validators` | The validators unit owns the application's PDF content validation. <sup>[1](../backend/src/common/validators/DOCS/Validators.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-validators.cb5529be)</sup> It exposes validatePdfContent, which validates a PDF buffer and detects the schedule mode from the first page's keywords, and isPdfValidUpSchedule, a non-throwing wrapper that reports validity and the detected type. <sup>[2](../backend/src/common/validators/DOCS/Validators.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-validators.a52803bf)</sup> <sup>[3](../backend/src/common/validators/DOCS/Validators.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-validators.b49da522)</sup> The upload service relies on validatePdfContent to determine the PDF type of uploaded files. <sup>[4](../backend/src/common/validators/DOCS/Validators.evidence.md#research.backend-src-common-validators.ef7d2a73)</sup> |
